questions.q: How is sound produced and how does it travel?
answer: Sound is produced by vibrating objects, that is, by a rapid to-and-fro motion.

answer.text: When an object vibrates, it makes the particles of the medium around it vibrate too, and this disturbance travels outward as sound. In human beings, sound is produced by the voice box, or larynx, using the vocal cords.

Sound needs a material medium — solid, liquid or gas — to travel through, and it cannot pass through a vacuum. This is why there is no sound in outer space. Sound travels fastest through solids and slowest through gases.

answer: It reaches our ears, which convert the vibrations into signals the brain understands as sound.

questions.q: Distinguish between pitch and loudness, and explain the audible range and noise pollution.

answer.text: Pitch, or shrillness, depends on the frequency of the sound, measured in hertz — a higher frequency gives a higher pitch, as in a whistle, and a lower frequency a low pitch, as in a drum. Loudness depends on the amplitude of the vibration, a larger amplitude giving a louder sound, measured in decibels.
Humans can hear sounds between 20 hertz and 20,000 hertz. Sounds below this are infrasonic and above it ultrasonic, which animals like dogs and bats can hear.
Unpleasant, loud sounds cause noise pollution, which harms health by causing hearing loss, stress and sleeplessness; it can be reduced by planting trees and controlling traffic and loudspeakers.
